title: The strict transform with respect to a composite blowing up is the iterated strict transform

standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of the strict transform of a quasi-coherent module and of a scheme with respect to a blowing up, by taking the image of the pullback of the module and the closure of the preimage of the complement of the centre
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the objects being compared and the surjections that generate them.

standard_prerequisites.name: The strict transform statement for two different centres, in the form that a strict transform acquires no nonzero sections supported on a prescribed centre given an effective Cartier divisor on it
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the iterated strict transform has no sections supported on the union of the two centres, which is the last step.

standard_prerequisites.name: Right exactness of pullback, so that the two defining surjections compose into a single surjection from the pullback of the module
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the two surjections onto the iterated strict transform and onto the strict transform with respect to the composite whose kernels have to be compared.

core_obligations: Set up the comparison: write the strict transform of the module with respect to the first blowing up, then the strict transform of that with respect to the second, and compare both with the strict transform with respect to the composite blowing up; by right exactness of pullback the two defining surjections combine into a surjection from the pullback of the module, and the strict transform with respect to the composite gives a second surjection from the same sheaf, so it suffices to compare the two kernels (proof lines 8991-9006).

Locate the kernels: the kernel of the first defining surjection is supported on the preimage of the first centre, hence after pullback it is supported on the preimage of the first centre again, while the kernel of the second is supported on the preimage of the second centre; thus the kernel of the composed surjection is supported on the preimage of the union of the two centres, which is the preimage of the closed subscheme defining the composite centre, so the composed surjection factors through the strict transform with respect to the composite (proof lines 9008-9027).

Conclude by the different-centres statement: it remains to see that the iterated strict transform has no nonzero local sections supported on the preimage of the union of the centres, which follows by applying the strict transform statement for two different centres to the first strict transform over the first blowing up, with the second centre and the preimage of the first centre as an effective Cartier divisor; the analogous statement for the strict transform of the scheme follows in the same way (proof lines 9028-9034).
proof_roadmap: Compare the two candidate strict transforms through the two surjections from the pullback of the module and reduce to equality of kernels (proof lines 8991-9006).

Show both kernels are supported on the preimage of the union of the centres and that the iterated strict transform has no sections supported there, using the two-centres statement (proof lines 9008-9034).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a blowing up which is exhibited as a composite of two blowing ups, the strict transform of a quasi-coherent module, and likewise of a closed subscheme, with respect to the composite equals the iterated strict transform with respect to the two steps (statement lines 8969-8989). The counted proof is a genuine sheaf-theoretic argument: it compares the two candidate transforms through two surjections from the pullback of the module, locates the supports of the relevant kernels on the preimages of the two centres, shows that the composed surjection factors through the strict transform with respect to the composite, and concludes by invoking the statement for two distinct centres to see that no nonzero sections are supported on the preimage of the union (proof lines 8991-9034). It is H2: the comparison and the support analysis are carried out in the counted span, with the cited input being the two-centres strict transform statement.
